subject: Rolling p95 spike — customer update, containment, and follow-up
messages:
From: Allegra Ramos <allegra.ramos@edgewarelabs.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Increased p95 latency — are you seeing this on your side?

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Over the last ~45 minutes we started seeing a sharp rise in P95 generation latency for our production calls to /v1/generate. Baseline p95 is ~380ms; we're seeing sustained ~1.6s and intermittent spikes toward 3.2s. A few requests time out on our side.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is reporting an active incident? Our engineers have started throttling retries but wanted to check if this aligns with any known capacity signal or regional routing change — we’re primarily routed to us-west.

Attached is a short histogram from our traces.

Thanks,
Allegra
Senior Platform Engineer
Edgeware Labs
[Attachment: client_p95_hist.zip (application/zip), 68KB]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Increased p95 latency — are you seeing this on your side?

Hi Allegra — thanks for the heads up and for the histogram. We're seeing correlated p95 elevations in our us-west model pool and have opened INC-7892 on the status page (link below).

What I can share right away:
- Scope: a rolling p95 surge affecting hosted generation traffic in us-west (some routed traffic to dedicated customers also observed).
- Impact: elevated p95 and a small fraction of timeouts on longer prompt workloads.
- Mitigation in progress: routing tier has begun gradual fanout to warm pools in us-central; an automated fallback to a slightly smaller model variant was enabled for latency-sensitive routes.

Immediate next steps for you:
1) If you can, temporarily reduce max_tokens or split long prompts to reduce per-request processing time.
2) If you need, we can pin your traffic to a dedicated fallback variant for the next 6 hours — I can coordinate that with Ben.

Status links: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/INC-7892
I've also opened an internal ticket and looped Ben (ops) to monitor backend queue depth. I'll follow up with a short timeline once we have containment confirmed.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: quick notes on mitigation steps (INC-7892)

Ben / Irene — quick running log from ops: 
- 09:05 PST: Observed a sustained increase in p95 and token queue depth on us-west pool gw-usw1-gpu-3.
- 09:12 PST: Autoscaler attempted to spin additional nodes but encountered delayed kernel compilation for a small subset of models (latency due to quantized kernel JIT warm).
- 09:20 PST: Enabled routing fanout to us-central warm pools and toggled model fallback policy for latency-sensitive routes (model: small-v2 as fallback).
- 09:36 PST: Prefix cache warming had a visible effect on shorter prompts; p95 decreased ~25%.
- 09:48 PST: Ongoing — tracking queue depth and attempt count.

Attachments: p95_snapshot_09-36.png (graph), quick-orch-playbook.md (playbook excerpt).

Marissa
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Allegra Ramos <allegra.ramos@edgewarelabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, security@edgewarelabs.com
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 16:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-containment summary and next steps (INC-7892)

Allegra / Edgeware team — thank you for your patience while we contained the issue. Below is a concise post-containment summary and the next steps toward a full postmortem.

Summary (what happened):
- Between ~09:00–10:05 PST on 2027-11-09 we observed a rolling p95 surge in the us-west hosted generation pool. Root cause: a temporary increase in kernel compilation latency for a small subset of quantized kernels on freshly-provisioned GPUs, which amplified token queueing when the autoscaler added capacity. That combination produced elevated tail latencies and occasional connection resets for requests that hit cold JIT paths.

Impact:
- Customers routed to us-west experienced elevated P95 (up to ~3.2s) and a small number of client-observed timeouts; error rates briefly increased for long-prompt workloads. No evidence that customer data was misrouted or exfiltrated. Internal logging shows no unexpected cross-tenant persistence.

What we did (containment):
1) Enabled warm-pool fanout to us-central to spread traffic and reduce pressure on kernel JIT paths.
2) Activated automatic model fallback to small-v2 for latency-sensitive routes.
3) Increased aggressive prefix cache pre-warming for commonly used prefixes.

Status now: normalizing. p95 has returned to baseline for the majority of workloads; we will continue to monitor through tomorrow.

Follow-up actions (next 72 hours):
- Ops will publish an internal timeline and the full postmortem doc by EOD Friday (2027-11-12).
- Engineering will implement a JIT-warmup handshake for newly-provisioned nodes to avoid cold-kernel spikes (week +2 plan).
- We will add an automated smoke-check during autoscaler scale-up to detect elevated kernel compile times and delay routing until warm.
- If Edgeware wants guaranteed isolation for critical routes during such events, we can scope a short-term dedicated fallback lane (ops can provide a cost estimate).

Links: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/INC-7892 (live incident view)
Internal ticket: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/INC-7892

Attachments included: p95_latency_graph.png (ops snapshot), incident-timeline-draft.pdf (initial timeline).

If you'd like a synchronous walkthrough of the postmortem or the mitigation playbook, I'm happy to set 30 minutes tomorrow.

Thanks again — apologies for the disruption.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
